slides.title: Versions
slides.notes: But first… let’s talk about the concept of VERSIONs.

slides.title: Introduction
slides.body:
Introduction
Versions
Versions are used to keep track of different improvements in a piece of software
slides.notes:
Now… in general, whenever we talk about software… 
We know that there will always be new improvements in whichever software we use. 
So… these improvements are released to the public as a new “version” of the software. 

In simple terms… 
Versions are used to keep track of different improvements in a piece of software

Let’s take an example to understand this better. 

If you’re a mobile phone user… there are chances that you may be using an Android-based mobile phone. Some people may use iOS too… 

Based on the year you bought your mobile phone and how frequently you update it… you will be a having a different version of the Android OS on your mobile. 
Android 8, 9, 10.0, 11.0, and most recently Version 14 and 15. 

This basically means… the software is getting multiple improvements and the corresponding updates, are packaged into a new version…

slides.notes:
So… since its release… HTML5 has introduced various new features like 
Multimedia support, 
Semantic Elements 
Geolocation features, etc. 
Support for new input types and much more. 

Moreover, HTML5 is fully supported by all modern browsers.

Let’s take a look at these features briefly

slides.title: Features of HTML5
slides.body:
Multimedia Support
HTML5 introduced native multimedia support with the <audio> and <video> tags
slides.notes:
Starting with Multimedia support. 

Multimedia, in simple terms… is anything that you can see or hear on a webpage. 

And HTML5 introduced native multimedia support with the <audio> and <video> tags

slides.body: Video & Audio Support

HTML5 introduced semantic elements such as <header>, <footer>, and <nav>, which enhances web page structure and accessibility

And when you use Semantic elements… the readability, and layouting of the web page gets much better. In simple terms… Semantic elements  enhances web page structure 
and accessibility

For example… on the left side, we have a semantic-elements based structure. 
And on the right, we only have div elements, which represent containers. 

From an accessibility and readability perspective, it’s really easy for us to understand the structure on the left side. We can easily point out what’s the header part, what’s the body section, where’s the footer, etc. 

We’ll learn more about semantic elements in later sessions.

slides.title: Features of HTML5
slides.body:
Location Support
Enables websites to access user’s geographical location via geolocation API
slides.notes:
Moving on… 

HTML5 also provides a Location support feature. 

This basically enables Enables websites to access a user’s geographical location via a geolocation API. 

For example: when we search for weather forecast on google, google automatically detects our city and provides you with forecast

Here… API = application programming interface, and it acts like an intermediary between two applications, that is… it allows two applications to talk to each other.
